rationale: A genuine change in economic content of the moat leg rather than a window tweak, though it sits awkwardly with the companion screen — an EBITDA-margin floor mechanically penalises the very expensed R&D/advertising that the commitment leg rewards, so the two legs may partly offset and any result will need that diagnosis.

This reverses a lesson the archive already learned and documented at generation 1 (ValueWithAssetScaledIntangibleRamp explicitly moved off sales because intangible-to-sales inflates mechanically when revenue collapses, importing distressed firms into the long leg), so it is a denominator swap back to a formulation already found inferior rather than a new mechanism.

The substituted leg is essentially Novy-Marx gross-profits-to-assets with intangibles netted out, so the signal reduces to the canonical value-plus-gross-profitability combination with a spending screen attached, and it also drops the time-series-floor construction that distinguished the archive's better moat proxies without arguing why a static level is preferable.

Internally inconsistent: book equity already nets all liabilities, so subtracting net debt again double-counts leverage rather than measuring "value accruing to equity," and it will drive the numerator negative for many levered firms, making the resulting cross-sectional ranking non-monotonic in cheapness.

Coherent and correctly motivated by two separate archive results, and the point that a cumulative stock tolerates sparse advertising disclosure better than a worst-year floor is a real advantage, but the construction is only the union of two already-tested modifications and should be judged incremental unless it clears the 8.8% alpha benchmark.

A legitimate additivity test that is explicitly aimed at the archive's alpha-versus-precision tension, but mechanically it is a one-term change to FirmLevelTangibleCapitalValue, so it is only worth the slot if the equity-versus-enterprise alpha gap is actually diagnosed (leverage/cash exposure in the denominator) rather than merely re-measured.
